name: Myeloid/Lymphoid Neoplasm Associated with JAK2 Rearrangement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues (2016)

criteria.description: Presence of JAK2 gene rearrangement confirmed by molecular genetic testing
Evidence of myeloid and/or lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia or other hematologic abnormalities
Exclusion of other myeloproliferative neoplasms and lymphoid malignancies without JAK2 rearrangement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Detection of JAK2 rearrangement in a myeloid or lymphoid neoplasm with compatible clinical and hematologic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of molecular, hematologic, and morphologic findings.

pathognomonic.notes: Elevated eosinophil count is a hallmark feature
searchTerms: high levels of eosinophils in blood
elevated white blood cells called eosinophils

pathognomonic.notes: Enlarged spleen due to extramedullary hematopoiesis

common.notes: Normocytic or macrocytic anemia frequently observed
Platelet counts may be decreased or elevated

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)

common.notes: Variable degree of fibrosis in marrow biopsy
searchTerms: scarring and thickening of bone marrow
bone marrow replaced by fibrous tissue

occasional.notes: Enlarged lymph nodes may be present
Liver enlargement due to infiltration or extramedullary hematopoiesis

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to CNS involvement
searchTerms: neurological symptoms from brain or spinal involvement
nerve problems due to central nervous system disease
brain or spinal cord related neurological signs

rare.notes: Rare complication secondary to vascular involvement
Rare kidney dysfunction related to disease or treatment

laboratory: Bone marrow biopsy showing myeloid/lymphoid proliferation with fibrosis
imaging: Splenomegaly and hepatomegaly on abdominal ultrasound or CT
Lymphadenopathy on CT or PET imaging
genetic: Detection of JAK2 gene rearrangement by FISH, RT-PCR, or NGS
other: Exclusion of other myeloproliferative neoplasms and lymphoid malignancies
Clinical correlation with eosinophilia and organ involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Variable eosinophilia without characteristic gene fusions
Different clinical course and treatment response

redFlags: Severe unexplained eosinophilia with organ dysfunction
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the WHO classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Orphanet: Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm associated with JAK2 rearrangement. ORPHA:589542.
Gotlib J. World Health Organization-defined eosinophilic disorders: 2017 update on diagnosis, risk stratification, and management. Am J Hematol. 2017.
